sample_unit: OCT volumes (753 participants) in the prospective Vietnam study
models_evaluated: federated learning–based 3D deep learning DME detection model with test-time adaptation and dual-threshold uncertainty

links.outcome: Prospective real-time performance of DME detection model in DR screening program
links.effect: Accuracy 93.70%, sensitivity 91.78%, specificity 93.06% for DME detection; performance similar to human experts.
links.quote: Our DL model was effective in detecting DME from three-dimensional OCT scans in a prospective, real-time clinical setting, suggesting that successful deployment of DL to improve DR screening programs in lower- and middle-income countries can be achieved.

links.outcome: Flagging uncertain cases for ophthalmologist re-evaluation via dual-threshold uncertainty range
links.effect: Model identified 64 cases as uncertain, indicating a need for re-evaluation by an ophthalmologist.
links.quote: In addition, the model identified 64 cases as uncertain, indicating a need for re-evaluation by an ophthalmologist.

unlisted_practices: federated learning for privacy-preserving model development
test-time adaptation to improve generalizability to unseen sites

screen.reason: The study prospectively validated a deep learning model for OCT DME screening in a live clinical setting in Vietnam and evaluated an uncertainty range safeguard (dual thresholds to flag uncertain cases for ophthalmologist re-evaluation).

primary.practice: uncertainty range dual-threshold flagging for clinician review
